items.title: Hawaii to Put Thirty Years of Eucalyptus Through Load Testing - Wood Central
items.body:
原话：“We can help create a more resilient local building supply.”
论点：他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
论据：Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.authors: Jun Wang
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Wood Central） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: We can help create a more resilient local building supply.
items.topic_zh: 关于增强当地建筑材料供应的观点
items.claim_zh: 他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
items.evidence_zh: Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.article_body:
Eucalyptus stands across more than 34,000 acres of Hawaiʻi’s old sugar land, or 13,760 hectares, and no published data exists to tell a builder what a plank of lumber can hold. However, that could soon change thanks to a new University of Hawaiʻi project , which will see the USDA Forest Service provide US$300,000 to generate structural design values for the species, with the project to fell the trees, saw the boards, and test them.
“We can help create a more resilient local building supply,” said Jun Wang, an assistant professor in the university’s Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering, whose team will run the work with state agencies, forest landowners, and industry partners. Wang has taken an additional $8,000 from the American Society for Engineering Education to incorporate the same material into civil engineering coursework at Mānoa.
Hawaiʻi’s large landowners put those trees into former cane land through the 1990s, holding tens of thousands of Hāmakua Coast acres off the property market , with agreements drawn to sell the crop to Oji Paper and Marubeni , the Japanese consortium that would chip it for paper. Hawaiian authorities rejected a 1997 lease over 4,150 hectares of public land after local opposition. The ventures that followed came and went, and the trees stayed.
Engineers cannot specify a beam without published design values, and no building official approves a species for load-bearing work until those numbers exist, regardless of what the timber does in a test rig. Eucalyptus grandis and E. saligna dominate the Hāmakua stands, which Mālama Hāmakua reports foresters rate suitable for flooring, structural, veneer, and ply work.
Distributors on the islands hold two to four weeks of stock compared with eight to 12 weeks on the mainland, so a West Coast price rise reaches an island invoice inside a fortnight, according to Associated Builders and Contractors Hawaiʻi. The same association puts local sourcing at under 20 per cent of the state’s building material needs, with the balance requiring an ocean crossing before reaching a site.
No mill on Hawaiʻi Island runs at the scale that would put eucalyptus boards alongside imported product on price, and the island’s hardwood mills stay with high-value koa to turn a profit, on Mālama Hāmakua’s account of what foresters told it. The wood that did leave between 2012 and 2016 went to China as veneer material before that market fell away, and a Waiakea mill licensed to peel the species never reached the volumes proposed.
It comes as Australian researchers turned plantation bluegum grown for pulp into structural glulam in February, the same class of timber used for the same purpose, with a Portland hub costing $200 million proposed to make the product at scale. Grading the timber and building the mill are separate bills, and only the first has been funded in Hawaiʻi.
Fire has given the state a second argument for cutting the stands, with the Department of Land and Natural Resources estimating that the 2012 Kōkeʻe wildfires released 72,000 tonnes of carbon, which it compares to the annual emissions of 18,000 cars. Those fires burned more than 3,000 acres of a Timber Management Area that covers 17,092 acres and holds more than 1,600 acres of eucalyptus and pine.
The department built a house from these species eight years ago, with Hale Liʻi framed in Sydney gum, rose gum, and southern yellow pine cut from Kōkeʻe on Kauaʻi and Hāmakua on Hawaiʻi Island. That 2018 grant came from the same federal Wood Innovations programme, and the 400-square-foot result is one nobody can yet repeat at commercial scale.
Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing, on an estate the university puts at over 34,000 acres. Design values will settle whether Hawaiʻi’s eucalyptus can be built with, and a mill will settle whether it ever is.
items.title_zh: 夏威夷将对三十年桉树进行负载测试

items.l1_lead: 夏威夷研究团队将对三十年桉树进行负载测试，以提升当地建筑材料的韧性，为建筑行业提供更可靠的材料支持。
items.l2_summary: 夏威夷的一项研究计划正在进行，旨在通过对三十年生桉树（Eucalyptus）进行负载测试，以增强当地建筑材料的韧性。该研究由Wang教授领导，获得了30万美元的资金支持，计划生成过去三十年未曾获得的数据。这项研究的核心论点是，通过科学研究可以提升夏威夷建筑材料的韧性，从而为当地建筑行业提供更可靠的材料支持。研究团队希望通过对桉树的负载测试，获取有关其物理特性和性能的数据，这些数据将为建筑材料的选择和应用提供重要的科学依据。通过这一研究，夏威夷的建筑行业将能够在材料的选择上更加科学和合理，进而提高建筑的安全性和耐用性。总之，这项研究不仅有助于填补过去三十年在建筑材料韧性方面的数据空白，还将为夏威夷的建筑行业带来积极的影响。

items.body:
原话：“1 in 4 autistic people have planned or attempted suicide. That’s why I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Professor Jason Arday who is autistic.”
论点：他对自闭症人士的关注是因为1/4的自闭症患者曾计划或尝试自杀。

items.article_body:
Sam Kahn Aug 03, 2026 373 15 58 Share Cambridge University’s Senate House. (Photo by Joe Giddens/PA Images via Getty Images.) This is a nasty story.
In 2023, Jason Arday made international news for becoming, at age 37, the youngest black professor in the history of Cambridge University. It wasn’t just that, though. Arday had a really remarkable background. Raised on a council estate in south London, Arday was, in his account, diagnosed at age three with autism and global development delay and didn’t speak until he was 11. At that point, something “clicked,” as he has put it, but he wouldn’t read or write until he was 18.
Then, Arday really applied himself. By age 30, he obtained a Ph.D. in Educational Studies from Liverpool John Moores University, and, according to his official biography , worked at Roehampton, Durham, and Glasgow before being appointed to a highly prestigious professorship at Cambridge. In his spare time, Arday was an ultra long-distance runner, in 2010 completing 30 marathons in 35 days and over two decades raising £5.5 million for charity.
It’s a beautiful story—Arday himself for the documentary “Great Big Story” said of his life, “Wouldn’t it be the most ridiculous story ever told?”—and it’s about to be commemorated in a memoir that Simon & Schuster UK is releasing later this month.
The only problem is that large portions of it may not be true.
In 2023, only months after his appointment at Cambridge, a pair of academics, Dave Harris and Martyn Hammersley, raised concerns to Cambridge, to Liverpool John Moores, and to different journals Arday had published in about the academic integrity of Arday’s work. Two of the journals issued corrections . Cambridge replied that the issues preceded Arday’s hiring and therefore were not within Cambridge’s “remit” to investigate. Liverpool John Moores, for its part, has issued a statement that the university in 2025 conducted a “confidential procedure” in response to the allegations and that “Professor Arday’s PhD still stands.”
Persuasion is a registered nonprofit that relies on reader support to pay our staff and keep our content free for everyone. If you value our work and want to fight for liberal values wherever they are threatened, please become a paying subscriber today!
In 2025, the Times Higher Education spiked an article about the allegations against Arday after Arday enlisted the defamation law firm Carter-Ruck to send a letter to the publication. But last month, Nathan Cofnas, a former Fellow at Cambridge, published a post on Substack that blew the Arday story wide open. Using the plagiarism detector Copyleaks, Cofnas found over 30 cases of “substantial overlap” in Arday’s Ph.D. dissertation with the previously-published dissertation of Paula Zwozdiak-Myers , many of them long chunks of verbatim copying, as well as verbatim copying from other sources. Cofnas went through ten other papers of Arday’s, taken from Arday’s own list of “principal and recent publications,” and found significant issues, including plagiarism, in at least four of them. Additional malfeasance included virtually identical quotes attributed to different sources in different papers, which strongly implies that at least some of the quotes from supposed participants in his studies were confabulated .
Meanwhile, Cofnas raised difficult questions about aspects of Arday’s personal story. He noted that running 30 marathons in 35 days would place Arday in the ultra-marathon elite—this without having left any ostensible mark in the running community. “If Arday [did that], I’ll eat my yarmulke,” said Cofnas by telephone. The claim to have raised £5.5 million for charity has already been walked back by Arday, who in a recent interview said the fundraising was done in conjunction with collectives. And Cofnas found that Arday’s two GCSE qualifications—in physical education and textiles—were unobtainable without passing written tests, a detail that challenges the timeline given by Arday that he could not read or write until he was 18. Cofnas also suggests that Arday’s account of his speech development is “medically improbable.”
Cofnas is far from a neutral party in this case. He was fired by Cambridge’s Emmanuel College in 2024 on the back of student protests against him for a Substack post in which he wrote that in a color-blind meritocracy “blacks would disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment.” Harris, the academic who first raised questions about Arday’s scholarship, was embroiled in a controversy of his own in which he had his emeritus title at Plymouth Marjon University stripped for a time after he critiqued critical race theory.
How To Fix DEI Rachel Kleinfeld · September 26, 2024 Read full story The fact that his accusers are controversial in their own right may help to explain why so many academics have reflexively defended Arday. In an interview with The Times of London, Arday this week said , “There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position. The motive is racially motivated. I think there’s a reason why it’s me, and I do think that reason is aligned to ableism and racism.” In 2025, when the allegations against Arday were beginning to surface, the Cambridge professors Simon Baron-Cohen and Ricardo Sabates circulated an open letter under the heading “URGENT PLEASE SIGN ANTI-RACISM LETTER FOR JASON ARDAY.” The Good Law Project, an activist organization, orchestrated a solidarity letter last week that has been signed by 14,000 people decrying the “sustained and malicious attacks on the academic integrity of Dr. Jason Arday,” which the letter attributed to “an attempt to undermine Black people who hold positions of influence.” And Cambridge University has wholeheartedly taken Arday’s side. A university spokesperson said , “Professor Arday has been the victim of a vile campaign to undermine his credibility, which must stop.”
So—as you can see—it’s an uncomfortable story landing right on the faultlines of the culture wars. On one side is institutional procedure alongside an institutional culture hyper-sensitive to accusations against what the Good Law Project calls “a working class Black man.” On the other side is the argument that standards must be maintained—and maintained by academic and journalistic vigilantes if the institutions are unwilling to uphold their own meritocratic principles.
And of course the real issue isn’t exactly Arday. It’s the presumption that the politically progressive culture ascendant at Cambridge and in higher education in general has long ago deviated from real meritocracy. By phone, Cofnas was clear on that point. He said, “This is a story about DEI and the corruption that is required to sustain the system of DEI—of elevating people based on identity characteristics rather than merit.”
So what do we do in a case like this, where everybody pretty much sees what they are already predisposed to see? Well, first of all, we look at the source material—and in this case it’s pretty unequivocal. For instance, Arday’s line on page 17 of his 2015 dissertation—“Student teachers are unique individuals and differ in their personal biographies and prior experiences, disposition to enquiry, cognitive and perceptive abilities, communication, interpersonal skills, adaptability, values, and belief systems”—is a perfect match to page 1 of Zwozdiak-Myers’ 2009 dissertation . According to Cofnas, the pattern is repeated dozens of times, while The Telegraph for its part found “more than 100 passages that are identical or nearly identical” to Zwozdiak-Myers’ thesis. There is, as Harris put it , “no other plausible explanation” than plagiarism for the overlaps.
Then, in the week following Cofnas’ Substack post, subsequent reporting found additional patterns of fabulism by Arday. In an open letter to a government minister last year, Arday said he was the victim of innumerable threats and attacks since he took up his Cambridge position. In an interview with The Guardian this week, Arday clarified that he was referring to, among other incidents, a “severed pig’s head” that had been sent to his parents’ London home. That assertion triggered a macabre scavenger hunt, with Guardian journalists visiting the butcher shop that Arday claimed had sold the pig to the assailant. But the butcher said that there had been no police investigation into the incident, as Arday had asserted. For their part, London’s Metropolitan Police said that the details Arday gave of a police investigation into the incident were “categorically” inaccurate.
Arday further claimed that a masked man had accosted him twice at his Cambridge faculty building and threatened him with a knife the second time. But as The Guardian noted, no intruder appeared on CCTV on either occasion, and Arday did not inform colleagues or interrupt his working day after the alleged knife incident.
Meanwhile, a recently-surfaced video interview with Arday appears to show him claiming that he starred in the acclaimed documentary “Seven Up”—a mathematical impossibility unless Arday was actually born in 1956. And just today Glasgow University has denied Arday’s claim that he held a visiting professorship there.
Given all that—the all-but-indisputable evidence of plagiarism, in addition to the patterns of fanciful statements by Arday—the case for his defense collapses. “I think it’s plagiarism and it’s obvious,” one academic told The Guardian under condition of anonymity. “There is no question that there is extensive plagiarism,” David Sanders, an independent researcher who reviewed Arday’s case last year for Times Higher Education , said to Retraction Watch.
What Being a Digital Nomad Taught Me About the Real World Sam Kahn · Jul 27 Read full story Arday, for his part, did not, in a wide-ranging interview he gave to The Times of London last week, directly challenge the primary allegation of plagiarism and academic misconduct. He said, “I am accountable for the mistakes I’ve made. I hold myself accountable and other people should hold me accountable.” Instead, he took another line of defense, contending, “We’re talking about academia here. I didn’t murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I’ve experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable.”
If it’s fair to say that the preponderance of evidence at this point speaks to serious academic misconduct on Arday’s part, the next question—picking up on Arday’s lead—is to ask ourselves what the stakes are here and what the story is really about. Arday is right of course that one academic with a shaky relationship to the truth is not, by itself, a huge deal. But, unfortunately for Arday’s defense, it is a story with more reach than he admits and it really does indict the institutions backing him.
For one thing, there is the issue of how Arday and his supporters have tried to defend him. There has been very little of the accountability Arday has called for—and there has been no willingness to look at the very obvious evidence of academic misconduct. The overriding tendency has been to shoot the messenger and to go after the academics, particularly Harris and Cofnas, who called attention to the issues in Arday’s work. According to The Guardian, Arday attempted to lodge a police complaint against Harris. Earlier this year, he dedicated a talk at the British Sociological Association to the “playbook” employed by conservative activists to target black professors. “There isn’t any room to sit there and watch your fellows suffer for no reason. It’s abhorrent, it’s a disgrace and, quite frankly, evil,” Arday said .
Apart from the often vitriolic counter-attack against Arday’s accusers, there has been a tendency to dodge the issue and shield Arday through arguments related to his neurodivergence. “1 in 4 autistic people have planned or attempted suicide. That’s why I’m very concerned about the impa
items.title_zh: 自闭症患者自杀风险引发关注
items.summary_zh: 文章提到，自闭症患者中有四分之一曾计划或尝试自杀，这一数据引发了对媒体报道影响的担忧。作者以自闭症人士Jason Arday为例，强调了对自闭症群体的关注，指出媒体在报道时应更加谨慎，以避免对这一脆弱群体产生负面影响。文章核心论点在于，社会应重视自闭症患者的心理健康问题，并采取措施降低自杀风险。
items.l1_lead: 自闭症患者中四分之一曾计划或尝试自杀，呼吁社会关注其心理健康并谨慎对待媒体报道。
items.l2_summary: 自闭症患者的心理健康问题日益受到关注，尤其是自杀风险的显著性引发了社会的广泛讨论。根据研究数据显示，约有四分之一的自闭症患者曾计划或尝试自杀，这一惊人的比例引起了人们对媒体报道的深刻反思。文章以自闭症人士Jason Arday为例，强调了对自闭症群体的关注，指出媒体在报道相关事件时应更加谨慎，以避免对这一脆弱群体产生负面影响。自闭症患者面临的心理健康挑战不仅影响他们的生活质量，也对社会的整体福祉构成威胁。因此，社会各界应当重视自闭症患者的心理健康问题，采取有效措施降低自杀风险。通过提高公众对自闭症的理解和支持，改善相关服务和资源的可获得性，可以为自闭症患者创造一个更安全、更包容的环境。总之，关注自闭症患者的心理健康，尤其是自杀风险，是社会责任的体现，亟需引起更多的重视和行动。

The figure suggests more than 20% of the company’s headcount has been affected, with the group’s last annual report showing it employed 505 staff as of September 30, 2025.
The online travel agent launched the 45-day consultation on March 26 , warning at the time that technology-driven efficiencies meant roles across the business were at risk.
A spokesperson for On the Beach confirmed on August 6 that the consultation had concluded, with 107 positions made redundant.
The business added that no staff were redeployed into alternative roles within the company.
An On the Beach spokesperson said: “Following the consultation process, 107 roles have been made redundant. Investment in technology has enabled us to automate and streamline a number of processes.
“These changes were made to drive operational efficiencies, deliver a better experience for customers and support our future growth.”
The redundancy process follows a period of strategic change for the group. In September 2025, On the Beach announced the closure of its Classic Collection B2B arm to focus on core B2C activities, a move that was met with sadness by the trade .
Speaking when the consultation was initiated in March, chief executive Shaun Morton said investment in technology meant several processes could be automated, putting roles at risk.
The push towards automation forms one of four primary strategic pillars outlined in the group’s annual report – alongside customer retention, expanding holiday choice, and trust – as it targets operational leverage across its tech platform.
Despite reporting a temporary downturn in demand earlier in the year following the outbreak of conflict in Iran, On the Beach has maintained its medium-term financial targets of £85 million in pre-tax profit and total transaction value (TTV) of £2.5 billion, alongside strong growth in direct app bookings.
The business posted its current record TTV for the year to last September, recording sales of £1.25 billion, up 11% year on year.

items.title: Warnings about Jason Arday’s mental health were ignored by the press - Good Law Project
items.body:
原话：“I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Jason Arday who is autistic.”
论点：媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能产生负面影响。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Good Law Project） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Jason Arday who is autistic.
items.topic_zh: 媒体报道对自闭症人士的影响
items.claim_zh: 媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能产生负面影响。
items.article_body:
We use cookies where necessary to allow us to understand how people interact with our website and content, so that we can continue to improve our service.
Dr Arday’s death was the direct result of media harassment – we’re demanding a public inquiry to prevent this from ever happening again
Before his death on Friday, Dr Jason Arday was subject to a barrage of racist, ableist and cruel media attention, which continued to escalate even after his resignation on August 5th.
The press attention was unrelenting. 249 articles were published in 22 days, mostly led by the broadsheets. This wasn’t a tabloid scandal – the journalists involved were often public figures in their own right.
A resignation normally causes the media to back off, but they only produced more content. Stories about Jason were driving clicks – with outlets like The Times even putting out paid adverts for their articles .
In his resignation letter, Dr Jason Arday said to his supporters “you have carried me through some of the darkest moments of my life”; “I need time to heal”; “space to begin again” and that he had “reached the limits of what any person should reasonably be expected to endure.”
Jason wasn’t the only one asking the press to stop.
Professor Simon Baron Cohen released a statement on July 31st, leaning on his expertise in autism, stating:
“I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Professor Jason Arday who is autistic.
He has been accused of plagiarism and he was cleared of any academic misconduct following a rigorous investigation by Liverpool John Moores University.
And yet he continues to be systematically discredited over every detail of his life, daily. We should of course always investigate plagiarism to protect academic standards.
However, I cannot stand by and watch when an autistic man is on the ground and the kicking continues. This is relentless bullying of a vulnerable autistic man and raises safe-guarding issues. It’s time to stop.”
The day afterwards, the Guardian published an article titled “Playbooks, plagiarism and a pig’s head: new claims surrounding a star Cambridge professor”.
Before this article was published, details of it were sent to Jason to give him an opportunity to respond. His supporters contacted The Guardian about this piece. A letter was sent to Katharine Viner, the Editor-in-Chief of the Guardian, and separate contact was made with the journalist writing the piece.
This article dissected Jason’s claims about his personal life, and the Guardian featured it on their podcast, Today In Focus. A reel the Guardian posted of that podcast, where the claims within the article were played for laughs, has since been deleted.
The Guardian’s coverage continued after Arday’s resignation, interviewing people who knew Jason as a child to question whether he was really non-verbal. The intense focus on Jason’s background and disability was widespread, with The Daily Mail even carrying a piece from a psychiatrist pondering a diagnosis for Jason, tempered only by the context that “I should say that I’ve never met Jason Arday, and so have no idea what has been going on in his mind, or how much truth there may or may not be in his life story.”
During the escalating coverage, those who supported Arday received countless requests for interviews and quotes.
These journalists were often warned about Jason’s wellbeing, and were still not dissuaded from chasing the story.
The writer and broadcaster Nels Abbey and Lord Simon Woolley , the Principal of Homerton College, both expressed their concerns.
Nels shared an example of this type of correspondence from the 3rd of August with a journalist during the firestorm, explicitly making clear his concern for Jason’s wellbeing.
Despite warnings from those around Jason trying to safeguard him from the onslaught, the stories kept coming.
Hours after Jason died, The Times ran a (now deleted) story headlined “Jason Arday may want to get himself a nice pair of orange trousers”.
Whilst this continued, the racist and eugenist academic Nathan Cofnas, who instigated the story, gave a little remarked upon interview to a right-wing youtuber, joking: “ After the revolution, I’ll be the head of the dept of eugenics & race science at Harvard.”
We believe that the press must be held accountable for their racist, profit-motivated conduct that led to Jason’s death. We’re calling for a public inquiry into how to ensure a responsible press given its contribution to Dr Arday’s tragic death.

items.title_zh: 媒体忽视Jason Arday心理健康警告的影响
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能带来的负面影响。文章引用了对Arday心理健康的担忧，指出媒体在报道中未能充分考虑其自闭症（autism）背景，可能加剧了对其的误解和偏见。专家强调，媒体的关注应更加谨慎，以避免对Arday及其他自闭症人士造成伤害。整体而言，文章呼吁媒体在报道此类敏感话题时，需更加关注受影响者的心理健康和社会影响。
items.l1_lead: 媒体在报道自闭症人士Jason Arday时忽视其心理健康背景，可能加剧误解与偏见，呼吁更谨慎的报道以保护受影响者。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能带来的负面影响，特别是对其心理健康的潜在威胁。文章指出，媒体在报道中未能充分考虑Arday的自闭症背景，导致对他的误解和偏见加剧。专家们强调，媒体在关注此类敏感话题时，应更加谨慎，以避免对Arday及其他自闭症人士造成进一步的伤害。报道中提到的心理健康担忧，反映了社会对自闭症人士的普遍误解，这种误解不仅影响了公众对他们的看法，也可能对他们的心理健康产生负面影响。

整体而言，文章呼吁媒体在报道涉及自闭症及相关心理健康问题时，需更加关注受影响者的心理健康和社会影响。通过对Arday案例的分析，作者希望引起媒体和公众对自闭症人士心理健康问题的重视，促使媒体在报道时采取更为负责任的态度，以减少对自闭症人士的偏见和误解。

items.title: Cambridge professor says university should continue Jason Arday investigation - The Independent
items.body:
原话：“They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.”
论点：大学应该让对Jason Arday的调查继续进行。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（The Independent） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.
items.topic_zh: 关于大学对Jason Arday事件的调查
items.claim_zh: 大学应该让对Jason Arday的调查继续进行。
items.article_body:
A fundraiser for Prof Arday’s family, set up by Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, has raised more than £60,000
Bookmark Bookmark popover Removed from bookmarks
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.
At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
The University of Cambridge ought to proceed with its probe into how Professor Jason Arday was recruited and his period teaching at the institution, according to a friend and former colleague.
Prof Arday, who was found dead on Friday, stepped down from his post as professor of sociology of education last week following allegations of plagiarism made against him.
Prior to his death, the university stated that it would look into the circumstances surrounding his "appointment and tenure", with the conclusions feeding into a wider review of senior recruitment processes.
It is understood that the university currently feels it would not be right to decide whether to continue the inquiry while Prof Arday’s family is grieving.
Sir Simon Baron-Cohen, a friend and former colleague of Prof Arday, told Times Radio that the university should "always be reflecting on how it’s operating and whether it can do better".
The Cambridge professor and director of the Autism Research Centre said: “They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.
“We should we should see what we learn from it. This is the whole purpose of investigations.
“When you’re talking about what’s in the public interest, when you’ve got public bodies like universities or, arguably, the media, political institutions, whatever, when we have investigations, it’s all about how can we improve them.”
Sir Simon said the professor’s mental health had been left “in tatters”, adding there were questions about whether the media failed in its duty of care towards him as a vulnerable person with disabilities.
He said the professor faced racist abuse and was used as a “lightning rod for a culture war on DEI (diversity, equity and inclusion)”.
“(Prof Arday) started reporting racism within weeks of him being at Cambridge,” Sir Simon said.
“It included things like threats of physical assault to himself and his family, racist hate speech, and racist actions, hate actions.”
Lord Simon Woolley, principal of Homerton College, Cambridge, and a former mentor of Prof Arday, told BBC Radio 4’s Broadcasting House programme that his friend felt “hounded to death”.
Lord Woolley said: “In a conversation I had with Jason on the Monday – we met on Monday, with a few dear friends – he said he felt hounded to death, his words, that he couldn’t see a way out.”
He added: “On that day, we saw a man half his body weight and desperate beyond belief.”
The crossbench peer said Prof Arday had been subjected to “the most horrendous, toxic, vicious witch hunt”, and called for an investigation into the “vicious media onslaught”.
“The whole of the black community and black academics have been brought into this debate as though we don’t belong in these positions, because we are collectively the diversity, equity and inclusion hires,” Lord Woolley added.
A fundraiser for Prof Arday’s family, set up by Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, has raised more than £60,000.
The organisation Stand Up To Racism has announced plans for a vigil for Prof Arday to be held on the steps of the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square, central London, at 6pm on Monday.
On Saturday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the professor’s death as a “tragedy on so many levels”, adding: “It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this.”
In a statement issued by his publisher Simon & Schuster UK on Friday, Prof Arday’s family said he had been subjected to a “campaign of sustained abuse” since he accepted the role of professor at Cambridge.
They said: “The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone.”
items.title_zh: 剑桥教授支持继续对Jason Arday的调查

items.l1_lead: 剑桥大学教授支持继续对Jason Arday的调查，强调学术界应保持严谨态度，确保公正透明，以维护学术诚信和大学声誉。
items.l2_summary: 剑桥大学的一位教授近日表示，大学应继续对Jason Arday的调查，以确保这一过程的公正和透明。他强调，调查已经启动，应该顺利进行，以便对所有相关问题进行充分审查。这一观点反映了学术界在处理类似事件时所应保持的严谨态度，突显了对学术诚信的重视。教授认为，调查的结果不仅关乎个体的声誉，更将对大学的整体声誉和未来发展产生重要影响。因此，继续推进调查显得尤为重要，以确保所有相关问题都能得到妥善处理，维护学术界的信任和公信力。

items.title: Jason Arday death 'tragedy on so many levels' says PM - BBC
items.body:
原话：“He was an incredibly, kind and gentle and caring man.”
论点：Jason Arday是一个非常善良和温柔的人。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen

quotes: He was an incredibly, kind and gentle and caring man.
items.topic_zh: 对Jason Arday的评价
items.claim_zh: Jason Arday是一个非常善良和温柔的人。
items.article_body:
Share Save Add as preferred on Google Ruth Comerford Death of Jason Arday 'a tragedy on so many levels', says PM Andy Burnham has described the death of former Cambridge professor Jason Arday as "a tragedy on so many levels", as he called for a "moment for reflection".
Arday was found dead at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday afternoon.
"It's not a moment for any rushing to judgement. It's a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this," the prime minister told broadcasters during a visit to Cornwall.
In a statement issued by his publisher Simon & Schuster UK, Arday's family said they were "in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son".
They said a "campaign of misinformation" had been too much for him.
Arday, 41, resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week after allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. He had denied the claims.
A friend told the BBC Arday had described feeling "destroyed" and had told him his authorisation to travel to the US had been revoked.
Eamonn McCrystal, who became his friend at St Mary's University, Twickenham, tried to reassure him what he was going through would pass, but Arday replied "it does not feel like it will."
McCrystal told the BBC "He was the nicest person. So kind and such a gentle soul.
"We shared an office at university, when I set up the student radio station, and he used to speak on the station a lot."
The University of Cambridge vice-chancellor Prof Deborah Prentice led the tributes, saying the faculty was "desperately saddened" to learn of his death.
"Our heartfelt sympathies go to Jason Arday's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time," she added.
Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "deeply shocked and saddened" and urged people to "remember there are real people with loved ones involved".
Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan said Arday was subjected to unrelenting media scrutiny.
He said he had faced "an unacceptable public hounding and campaign of abuse" and was the victim of "a pernicious public shaming".
"His death was a tragedy, but once again it should be a wake up call for all of us," he posted on X.
A donation page, set up by Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, has raised more than £10,000 to help cover funeral costs for Arday's family.
"Today should be about compassion, dignity and solidarity with a grieving family," Vernon wrote.
"Jason's life was bigger than the controversy that surrounded his final weeks."
A vigil will be held on Monday evening on the steps of the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square, held by the organisation Stand Up To Racism.
The group's co-convenor, Weyman Bennett, said Arday's death "was the result of a racist witch hunt".
Jo Grady, general secretary of the University and College Union, said the "level of harassment he suffered and the racism he was subjected to has been sickening" and "must be investigated".
Lord Paul Boateng, who became the UK's first black cabinet minister in 2002, told BBC Newsnight he was "horrified, shocked and deeply saddened".
"Racism in academia is a fact of life and needs to be addressed," he added in a written statement.
In a statement on Saturday, National Education Union general secretary Daniel Kebede said Arday had been subjected to "a public and brutal takedown that unleashed a tirade of racism".
"The effect has been chilling. It tells black people and others from underrepresented backgrounds that entering prominent public positions will make you a target," he said.
Prof Simon Baron-Cohen, director of the Autism Research Centre at the University of Cambridge, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme Arday had been "bombarded by every media outlet to paint him as a fraud".
"He was an incredibly, kind and gentle and caring man," he said.
He spoke to Arday the morning of his death, and said the academic had felt unable to leave the house.
"He has experienced what he described as a campaign against him, for the last three years," he previously told BBC News.
"What he was saying to me was 'they've destroyed my life' - it's not clear who they were but I think he was referring to the media.
"The personal attacks on him have been so immense."
Former colleague of Arday says they spoke on morning of his death Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor of Black Studies Kehinde Andrews, a friend of Arday, described him as "very down" after resigning from Cambridge.
"He was very upset. He felt that there was no way out. He effectively wasn't leaving the house. He had lost a lot of weight," Andrews said.
"There should be a wakeup call to just how bad black academics actually have it in academia."
Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy also told the programme "the idea that an academic would be dragged through this amount of media scrutiny is unheard of".
On Saturday Scotland's First Minister John Swinney said that people who "made many hard comments must now consider the impact of their words", describing it as a "deeply concerning and very sad case".
Prior to his appointment at Cambridge, Arday had worked as a professor at the University of Glasgow.
Shadow communities secretary Sir James Cleverly said he was angered by the "tragic" death and said "a number of people at a number of academic institutions have serious questions to answer".
When asked by the BBC on Saturday if the University of Cambridge needed to answer questions over its duty of care, Cleverly said the university should "ask themselves how he got into this position, how he ended up being in the eye of the storm, what could and should have happened to prevent this long before it got to this tragic situation".
Arday had denied plagiarism - but admitted errors in his work - and said the recent controversy had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".
The row first erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in the professor's work.
Arday said some errors in his early academic work arose because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information. Similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics, he said.
Questions were also raised about parts of his life story, including that he ran 600 miles in six days and that he had raised £5.5m for charity.
He later said the run was actually completed over a 12-day period to allow for rest days - and that the huge sum was raised with the help of others.
Arday's appointment as Cambridge's youngest ever black professor at the age of 37 in 2023 was hailed at the time.
Announcing his resignation last week, Arday said the "personal cost" of the scrutiny of him had become "too great".
He said: "While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement.
"The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love."
He stressed that his resignation should not "be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me".
Earlier this week, Cambridge announced an independent investigation around the circumstances of Arday's appointment.
Liverpool John Moores University - which awarded Arday his PhD in 2015 - concluded that he had not plagiarised work.
In a statement on Saturday, a spokesperson for the university said it was "saddened to hear of the tragic loss of Professor Jason Arday".
Jason Arday speaks with former tutor in 2023 If you've been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line Additional reporting by Emma Vardy
items.title_zh: 杰森·阿尔代去世引发多重悲剧感慨
items.summary_zh: 杰森·阿尔代（Jason Arday）被描述为一个非常善良和温柔的人。英国首相在谈及他的去世时表示，这一事件在多个层面上都是一场悲剧。阿尔代的离世不仅让身边的人感到失落，也引发了对他所代表的价值观和人际关系的深思。他的善良品质和温柔性格使他在社会中留下了深刻的印记，令人惋惜。
items.l1_lead: 杰森·阿尔代的去世引发了对人际关系和社会价值观的深刻反思，令人感到多重悲剧的惋惜。
items.l2_summary: 杰森·阿尔代的去世引发了深刻的悲剧感慨，令人们对他所代表的价值观和人际关系进行了反思。阿尔代被描述为一个非常善良和温柔的人，这种品质使他在社会中留下了深刻的印记。他的离世不仅让身边的人感到失落，也让人们意识到善良和温柔在当今社会中的重要性。英国首相在谈及阿尔代的去世时指出，这一事件在多个层面上都是一场悲剧，反映了人际关系的脆弱和对美好品质的珍视。阿尔代的生活和价值观激励了许多人，他的离去让人们更加珍惜与他人之间的联系和情感。总的来说，阿尔代的去世不仅是个人的损失，更是社会对善良与温柔的深刻思考，提醒我们在日常生活中应更加关注和弘扬这些美德。

items.title: Polymeric Sorbents as Energy-Efficient Alternative to Cryogenic Distillation for Light Hydrocarbon Purification.
items.body: Light hydrocarbons are essential gaseous compounds for fuel, polymer manufacturing, fertilizer production, and so forth. The efficient recovery and purification of these gases are still challenging despite their significant industrial and domestic relevance. They exist in the gaseous state under ambient temperature and pressure and are typically recovered from natural gas streams containing multiple close-boiling-point hydrocarbons. So far, cryogenic distillation is the commonly used method for their separation and purification. It operates based on their boiling-point differences, which amounts to significant energy consumption. To address this limitation, adsorption-based technology is considered an energy-efficient alternative for the purification of light hydrocarbons. To this effect, polymeric sorbents such as porous polymer networks (PPNs) are a potential alternative due to their robustness, stability, and scalability. This review provides an extensive discussion on cryogenic distillation, applications of light hydrocarbons, and progress in light hydrocarbon purification using polymeric sorbents. Additionally, the pore structure, stability, and techno-economic feasibility of the polymeric sorbents were extensively examined, covering current progress, mechanism of guest molecule separation, characterization techniques, and hurdles still encountered. Overall, since their application in light hydrocarbon separation is still an evolving field, this review will facilitate robust designs by providing the necessary know-how and roadmaps needed for advancement.
items.authors: Festus K, Mondal A, Mandal S, Aiya D Marquez J, Ghosh A, Sikdar A, Podder U, Sarkar A, Wang Q, Zhou HC.
items.title_zh: 聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案
items.summary_zh: 轻烃是燃料、聚合物制造和肥料生产等重要气体化合物。尽管其在工业和家庭中的重要性，轻烃的高效回收和净化仍然面临挑战。当前，低温分馏（cryogenic distillation）是分离和净化轻烃的常用方法，但其能耗较高。为了解决这一问题，基于吸附的技术被认为是轻烃净化的节能替代方案。聚合物吸附剂，如多孔聚合物网络（PPNs），因其稳健性、稳定性和可扩展性而成为潜在选择。本文广泛讨论了低温分馏、轻烃的应用及聚合物吸附剂在轻烃净化中的进展，并详细考察了聚合物吸附剂的孔结构、稳定性和技术经济可行性，涵盖了当前进展、客体分子分离机制、表征技术及仍面临的挑战。
items.l1_lead: 聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案，展现出优越的稳定性和可扩展性，有望解决传统低温分馏方法的高能耗问题。
items.l2_summary:
轻烃是燃料、聚合物制造和肥料生产等多个领域的重要气体化合物，然而其高效回收和净化仍面临诸多挑战。目前，低温分馏（cryogenic distillation）是分离和净化轻烃的常用方法，但其能耗较高，限制了其广泛应用。为了解决这一问题，基于吸附的技术被提出作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案，其中聚合物吸附剂（如多孔聚合物网络，PPNs）因其优越的稳健性、稳定性和可扩展性而成为潜在的选择。

本文深入探讨了低温分馏的局限性、轻烃的广泛应用以及聚合物吸附剂在轻烃净化中的最新进展。聚合物吸附剂的孔结构、稳定性和技术经济可行性是其在轻烃净化中发挥作用的关键因素。研究表明，聚合物吸附剂能够有效地选择性吸附轻烃分子，进而提高净化效率。通过对客体分子分离机制的分析，本文揭示了聚合物吸附剂在不同条件下的表现，并利用多种表征技术对其性能进行了评估。

尽管聚合物吸附剂在轻烃净化中展现出良好的前景，但仍面临一些挑战，包括材料的长期稳定性、吸附选择性的优化以及大规模应用的经济性等。因此，未来的研究需要集中在提高聚合物吸附剂的性能和降低其生产成本上，以实现其在轻烃净化领域的广泛应用。总体而言，聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案，展现出良好的应用潜力，有望在未来的工业实践中发挥重要作用。

items.title: How will this year’s record breaking El Niño affect NZ and the world? 5 things to know
items.body: From global temperature records to drought risk in New Zealand, the developing climate pattern could have far-reaching consequences.
items.authors: Kevin E. Trenberth
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/kevin-trenberth-15259（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 今年创纪录的厄尔尼诺现象将如何影响新西兰及全球？
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了正在发展的厄尔尼诺现象（El Niño）对新西兰及全球的潜在影响。厄尔尼诺现象可能导致全球气温创纪录上升，并增加新西兰的干旱风险。文章指出，气候模式的变化可能会对农业、生态系统和水资源管理产生深远影响。科学家们警告，随着厄尔尼诺现象的发展，全球范围内的极端天气事件可能会增多，影响各国的经济和社会稳定。因此，了解这一气候模式的动态变化及其后果，对于制定应对策略至关重要。
items.l1_lead: 厄尔尼诺现象将导致全球气温上升和新西兰干旱风险增加，可能引发极端天气事件，影响农业、生态和社会经济稳定。
items.l2_summary:
今年，厄尔尼诺现象（El Niño）的发展引发了全球范围内的广泛关注，尤其是对新西兰及全球气候的潜在影响。厄尔尼诺现象的出现可能导致全球气温创纪录上升，这一变化不仅会影响气候模式，还可能加剧新西兰的干旱风险。文章指出，气候模式的变化将对农业、生态系统和水资源管理产生深远的影响，尤其是在新西兰这样一个依赖农业的国家，干旱的加剧可能会直接影响粮食生产和水资源的可持续利用。

科学家们警告，随着厄尔尼诺现象的持续发展，全球范围内的极端天气事件可能会显著增多。这些极端天气事件包括更频繁和更强烈的风暴、洪水和干旱等，可能对各国的经济和社会稳定造成严重威胁。对于新西兰而言，干旱的风险增加将直接影响到农作物的生长和水资源的分配，进而影响到国家的经济发展和民众的生活质量。

因此，了解厄尔尼诺现象的动态变化及其后果，对于制定有效的应对策略至关重要。各国政府和相关机构需要密切关注这一气候现象的发展，并采取相应的措施来减轻其可能带来的负面影响，以保障国家的经济安全和社会稳定。总之，厄尔尼诺现象的影响不仅限于气候变化本身，更是对全球生态、经济和社会结构的深远挑战。
items.l3_translation:
距离预计的高峰还有几个月，厄尔尼诺现象已经在推动海洋温度进入创纪录的领域。

七月带来了全球海面温度有史以来该月最高的记录，部分原因是这一快速发展的气候模式。最新的预测表明，未来还有更多的变化。

那么，厄尔尼诺究竟是什么？为什么这次的厄尔尼诺可能如此重要？这对新西兰意味着什么？以下是五个需要了解的要点。

厄尔尼诺是一种自然气候模式，涉及中部和东部热带太平洋海洋的异常升温，并伴随风和大气环流的变化。

以下是这一过程通常是如何运作的。太阳加热热带海洋，而信风则将温暖的表层水向西推送，穿过赤道太平洋，导致水在印度尼西亚、北澳大利亚和东南亚附近堆积。较冷的水从东太平洋下方上升。

这种堆积意味着西太平洋“暖池”的海平面平均比南美东部的东太平洋高出约60厘米。如果没有信风将其保持在那里，这些温暖的水将会向东流动。但堆积的量是有限的。

厄尔尼诺的启动方式各不相同，天气和热带风暴有时会削弱信风并提供触发因素。一旦开始，温暖的水开始向东涌向太平洋。

跨越海洋可能需要两到三个月的时间，随着水流的移动，雷暴和降雨也会发生变化，并影响远超热带太平洋的天气模式。

厄尔尼诺事件通常每两到七年发生一次，最常见的是每三到五年发生一次。海温通常在十二月达到峰值，最大的气候效应通常发生在次年的二月。

到2025年12月，热带太平洋已经为厄尔尼诺做好了准备。与热带风暴相关的西风脉冲帮助启动了这一过程，随后涌动的暖水进一步增强了朝向南美的升温。

今年年初，重大事件的迹象开始显现。前新西兰国家水与大气研究所气象学家Ben Noll在二月提出了这一可能性，到七月时警告称这可能成为一个非常强的——或称“超级”——厄尔尼诺。

当前的预测表明，这一事件将在年底前继续增强，热带太平洋关键区域的海面温度将达到超过创纪录的3°C高于平均水平。

厄尔尼诺的展开是在人为造成的升温背景下进行的，全球海洋热含量在2017年至2025年的每一年都达到了创纪录的水平。

1997-98年的厄尔尼诺事件使得1998年成为20世纪最热的一年。2015-16年的厄尔尼诺将温度推向了另一个水平，而在2023-24年的事件中，记录再次被刷新。

强厄尔尼诺事件会将一些积累的海洋热量释放到大气中，暂时提升全球表面温度。因此，全球温度可能呈现出阶梯状，主要的厄尔尼诺事件帮助将其推向逐步更高的台阶。

这一正在发展的厄尔尼诺可能提供下一个台阶，2026年全球温度可能创下新高，2027年更有可能。

气候变化如何影响厄尔尼诺仍然不确定。但有迹象表明，升温可能正在改变这一现象本身，可能增加非常强事件的风险。

厄尔尼诺对全球产生深远影响，影响干旱、洪水、风暴和热浪，以及农业、健康、渔业、野火风险和经济活动。

一些影响已经显现。干燥的条件扰乱了东南亚和中美洲部分地区的作物，而联合国世界粮食计划署估计，厄尔尼诺可能使到年底近5000万人面临急性饥饿。

厄尔尼诺的全球影响很大程度上来自其对降雨的影响。热带太平洋异常高的海面温度将降雨向海洋转移，往往导致陆地干旱。这些变化改变了大气环流和更远地区的天气模式，同时增加了干燥地区的野火风险。

温度和降雨的变化可能影响疟疾、登革热和霍乱等疾病。厄尔尼诺还会改变热带气旋活动，通常在太平洋的中部和东部增加活动，而在热带大西洋则抑制活动。

南美沿海的上升流减弱也减少了冷却、富含营养的水的供应，扰乱了海洋生态系统，并可能导致渔业和海鸟种群的急剧下降。

经济影响可能持续多年，有可能造成数万亿美元的损失。

新西兰已经经历了厄尔尼诺的一些影响，包括在这个冬季大部分时间里相对晴朗但寒冷的南风条件。

与世界许多地区不同，新西兰在厄尔尼诺期间通常会经历较凉的天气。

最强的影响通常在年末显现。在塔斯曼海对面，它可能导致澳大利亚大部分地区的干旱和野火风险，火灾产生的烟雾有时会飘到新西兰。

厄尔尼诺往往会给新西兰东北部，特别是北岛带来更干燥的条件，而西南部——包括峡湾地区和西海岸——则可能变得更湿润。

考虑到这一事件的潜在强度，新西兰面临所谓“干年”的真实风险，这将对农业和水电发电产生影响，并增加野火的风险。

农民和其他面临这些风险的人应为条件发展可能导致的干旱做好准备。

杰出学者，国家大气研究中心；奥克兰大学附属教员，Waipapa Taumata Rau

items.body:
原话：“If we are serious about reversing current trends, there is no single intervention that will solve the obesity problem, but several, in combination, could make a meaningful difference.” / “People living with obesity deserve compassionate, evidence-based care rather than judgment.” / “We cannot medicate our way out of an unhealthy food environment.”

items.evidence_zh: 几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人生活在肥胖中，增加了多种疾病的风险。
items.article_body:
Prof Naveed Sattar says the rise in obesity reflects profound changes in how people eat and move - Chris Watt Growing up in Glasgow in the late 1970s, life looked rather different from today. My local shop might have stocked only a handful of biscuit varieties, and a packet was often shared among the family over the course of a week. Most meals were cooked at home, there were far fewer cars on the roads, and many jobs involved considerably more physical activity than is common now.
We should be cautious about romanticising the past. Life was not necessarily better, but in one important respect it was different: the environment in which we lived made it easier to maintain a healthy weight. Daily life involved more movement, and there were far fewer opportunities to consume highly processed , energy-dense foods throughout the day.
Today, the picture is very different. Research I recently co-wrote, led by colleagues at the University of Cambridge, highlights how obesity has become one of the most important public health challenges facing our society. Nearly one in three adults in England now lives with obesity, which increases their risk of many conditions, including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease, sleep disorders, several cancers and musculoskeletal conditions, while placing growing pressure on an already stretched NHS.
Perhaps most concerning is that rates are rising faster among younger generations and those living in the most deprived communities. This rise is not a consequence of declining willpower, increased laziness or greater greed. Rather, it reflects profound changes in our food and activity environments that have made weight gain more likely across the population.
If we are serious about reversing current trends, there is no single intervention that will solve the obesity problem, but several, in combination, could make a meaningful difference.
Today, high-calorie foods and drinks are available almost everywhere: supermarkets, petrol stations, high streets and, increasingly, through food-delivery apps. They are heavily marketed, highly convenient and often relatively inexpensive. It is therefore unsurprising that many researchers now regard the food environment as a principal driver of rising obesity rates.
Governments, industry and public health organisations must work together to improve the nutritional quality of the foods available to us. Further legislative restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy products to children, continued reformulation to reduce excess sugar, salt and unhealthy fats, and incentives for companies to develop healthier products should all be pursued.
Improving the nation's health requires a better balance between commercial interests and critically important public health objectives. Ultimately, long-term success will depend on making healthier choices easier and less healthy choices harder.
Eating habits formed in childhood often persist into adulthood. Ensuring access to nutritious school meals can help improve dietary quality, particularly among children from disadvantaged backgrounds who may otherwise bring less nutritious food from home or buy fast food during their lunch break. Ensuring that every child has access to at least one healthier meal every weekday would require investment, but could pay dividends in the long run.
Equally important is practical nutrition education that helps young people understand food, develop cooking skills and appreciate that taste preferences can change over time, so that healthier foods can become highly enjoyable.
Ensuring children have access to nutritious school meals is key to improving dietary quality and instilling healthy eating habits, says Prof Sattar - Chris Watt
New and improved nutrition lessons should be introduced to support children in eating better. We also need more children to train in farming and food processing, so that future generations are interested in producing homegrown British fruit and vegetables. If more of our own produce is available on supermarket shelves, it could be fresher and more appealing, encouraging people to eat more of it. I know this will require investment, but if we want a healthier, fitter, happier nation, it needs to be done.
Physical activity deserves equal attention. Activity levels often fall sharply during adolescence, particularly during the secondary school years. Not every child enjoys competitive sport, and that is entirely reasonable, so schools should actively offer alternatives during PE lessons, such as walking, cycling, dance, outdoor pursuits and recreational games. All contribute to good health.
The goal should not be to create elite athletes; it should be to help young people discover forms of activity they genuinely enjoy. Countries that successfully embed movement throughout the school day, such as the Netherlands, offer useful lessons. Investment in facilities and community partnerships – such as collaborations between schools, leisure centres, charities and local health services to promote healthy eating and physical activity – would be money well spent, delivering benefits for decades to come.
Britain has a growing population of healthy retirees with valuable skills and life experience. With appropriate training, safeguarding and oversight, even occasional volunteering – perhaps once a month – could help support children's physical activity, outdoor learning and community programmes.
Regular movement improves both physical and mental wellbeing, yet around half of adults do not meet the NHS exercise recommendations. Creating communities that encourage activity should therefore be a public health priority. Safe walking and cycling routes and groups, well-maintained parks and green spaces, affordable leisure facilities and community programmes would all help.
Around half of UK adults fail to meet the NHS exercise recommendations
Importantly, opportunities for physical activity are not distributed equally. In affluent areas, people often enjoy better access to safe environments and leisure facilities. In more deprived communities, practical barriers can make regular activity far more difficult. Addressing these inequalities requires sustained local investment.
The public health message itself needs to be simplified. Rather than encouraging only ambitious goals, we should emphasise that even small increases in activity matter. An additional 500 to 1,000 steps a day is achievable for millions of people and could deliver health benefits. Even five to 10 minutes of extra walking each day can help people become more active and can be an achievable starting point.
People living with obesity deserve compassionate, evidence-based care rather than judgment. Obesity is not simply about willpower but is shaped by a complex interplay of genetics, early-life experiences and the environments in which people live, learn and work. People living with obesity should therefore be treated with empathy and respect.
Because obesity affects almost every area of healthcare, all healthcare professionals should receive training in its prevention and management, equipping them with practical lifestyle advice and a clear understanding of the treatments now available, so patients can make informed choices.
Every clinical encounter presents an opportunity to discuss weight sensitively and constructively. In my experience, supported by evidence from trials, most patients are willing to engage when these conversations are approached with empathy and respect.
Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) injections and tablets have demonstrated substantial weight loss and improvements in a range of obesity-related conditions. By reducing appetite and food cravings, as well as body weight, they give people the opportunity to think about and better adopt other lifestyle changes.
They are not, however, a substitute for obesity prevention. We cannot medicate our way out of an unhealthy food environment. However, they are becoming an increasingly important part of obesity care and offer genuine hope to many people who have struggled with their weight for decades.
The challenge now is ensuring fair and sustainable access. While some worry that private provision may worsen inequalities, there is another perspective. Those who can afford to pay privately may reduce pressure on NHS services, allowing limited public resources to be targeted towards those with the greatest need and the least ability to pay.
The NHS should also begin thinking differently about how these potentially disruptive medicines are managed. Given their likely effect on diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease and multiple other areas of medicine, there is a strong case for a single national body to oversee their implementation, coordinate access and monitor outcomes across the NHS. Such an approach could help ensure consistency, maximise value for money and collate fast real-world evidence of the drugs' effects.
A means-tested co-payment system, whereby some patients contribute towards the cost of treatment according to their ability to pay, could, in principle, stretch finite NHS resources further. This could enable more people to benefit while protecting access for those who would otherwise be unable to afford treatment. Given the scale of the obesity crisis, new approaches to financing effective therapies deserve serious consideration.
There may even be wider societal benefits. As more people use these treatments, demand for healthier foods and smaller portion sizes could encourage manufacturers and retailers to adapt their offerings in ways that benefit the broader population.
These are not the only answers, nor will every proposal prove equally effective, but together they illustrate the breadth of action likely to be needed if we are to give future generations a better chance of living healthier lives.
Professor Naveed Sattar is Professor of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the University of Glasgow and Honorary Consultant at Glasgow Royal Infirmary

items.title_zh: 英国肥胖问题亟需多重干预措施
items.summary_zh: 文章指出，英国肥胖率上升反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化，单一的干预措施无法有效解决这一问题。当前，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人生活在肥胖中，这显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家强调，若要逆转这一趋势，必须采取多种措施的结合，而非依赖药物治疗。同时，生活在肥胖中的人们应获得基于证据的关怀，而非评判。
items.l1_lead: 英国肥胖问题日益严重，需综合多重干预措施而非单一药物治疗，以有效应对饮食和活动环境的变化。
items.l2_summary: 英国的肥胖问题日益严重，反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化。根据最新数据，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人正面临肥胖的困扰，这一现象显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家们指出，单一的干预措施无法有效应对这一复杂的健康危机，因此必须采取多种措施的结合来逆转这一趋势，而不是单纯依赖药物治疗。当前的研究强调，生活在肥胖中的人们应当获得基于证据的关怀，而不是受到评判和歧视。这种基于证据的关怀不仅能够帮助个体更好地理解自身的健康状况，还能提供有效的支持和指导，促进健康生活方式的形成。综上所述，解决英国肥胖问题需要综合性的干预策略，以应对其背后的多重因素，而非简单依赖单一的解决方案。

items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。科学家指出，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素，但体重增加导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一观点强调了体重管理在2型糖尿病治疗中的重要性，提示我们在应对这一疾病时需要关注生活方式的改变和遗传因素的影响。
items.l1_lead: 2型糖尿病与体重增加和内脏脂肪密切相关，强调体重管理和生活方式改变在治疗中的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。研究表明，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素（insulin），但体重增加所导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一发现提示我们，体重管理在2型糖尿病的治疗中至关重要，尤其是在当前全球范围内，2型糖尿病的发病率持续上升的背景下。

科学家们指出，内脏脂肪的过度积累不仅会导致胰岛素抵抗（insulin resistance），还会引发一系列代谢紊乱，进一步加重糖尿病的病情。因此，控制体重、改善饮食习惯和增加身体活动成为了应对2型糖尿病的重要策略。此外，遗传因素也在2型糖尿病的发病机制中扮演着重要角色，某些基因的变异可能使个体更易于发展为糖尿病。

综上所述，本文强调了在应对2型糖尿病时，除了药物治疗外，生活方式的改变和对遗传因素的关注同样不可忽视。通过综合管理体重和改善生活方式，患者可以有效降低糖尿病的风险，改善健康状况，进入一个新的治疗纪元。

items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的发病机制，强调不同性别和种族在体重增加后发展糖尿病的风险存在显著差异。具体而言，平均男性需要增加的体重低于平均女性，而平均亚洲人需要增加的体重低于平均白人。作者指出，这一现象反映了遗传和生理差异对糖尿病风险的影响，提示在制定预防和治疗策略时应考虑这些因素。通过对这些差异的理解，未来的治疗方法可能会更加个性化和有效。
items.l1_lead: 2型糖尿病的发病机制受性别和种族影响，男性和亚洲人发展糖尿病所需的体重增加更少，提示治疗策略应更加个性化。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的发病机制，强调了性别和种族在体重增加后发展糖尿病风险方面的显著差异。研究表明，平均男性在体重增加后发展糖尿病所需的体重增加量低于平均女性，而平均亚洲人所需的体重增加量又低于平均白人。这一现象反映了遗传和生理差异对糖尿病风险的影响，提示在制定预防和治疗策略时应充分考虑这些因素。

具体而言，男性和女性在体重增加后的代谢反应存在差异，可能导致男性在较小的体重增加下就面临更高的糖尿病风险。此外，种族差异也表明，不同人群在体重增加后对糖尿病的易感性不同，亚洲人群在体重增加后更容易发展为糖尿病，这可能与其遗传背景和生理特征有关。

通过对这些差异的深入理解，未来的治疗方法可能会更加个性化和有效。个性化治疗不仅可以提高治疗效果，还能更好地满足不同人群的需求，从而在更大程度上降低糖尿病的发病率。因此，研究者呼吁在糖尿病的预防和治疗策略中，必须考虑性别和种族等因素，以制定更为精准的干预措施。这一研究为2型糖尿病的管理提供了新的视角，强调了个体差异在疾病发展中的重要性。

Taiwan's representative to Japan, Lee Yi-yang (second left), poses with members of a five-person Taiwanese delegation at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial in Japan on Thursday for the annual Peace Memorial Ceremony. Photo courtesy of Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Japan Tokyo, Aug. 6 (CNA) A Taiwanese delegation led by Taiwan's representative to Japan, Lee Yi-yang (李逸洋), joined representatives from 121 countries and regions at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony on Thursday.
In a news release, the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Japan quoted Lee as saying that after the world's first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima 81 years ago, killing about 140,000 people, many survivors suffered the lifelong effects of radiation exposure.
Lee said humanity must learn from the devastating consequences of war to prevent such tragedies from happening again and turn the collective memory of those disasters into a driving force for peace, stability and development.
Lee said he joined representatives from around the world in calling for a world free of nuclear weapons and the pursuit of lasting peace.
Lee also expressed condolences to those killed in the atomic bombing, noting that many Taiwanese who had been living, studying or serving in the Japanese military in Hiroshima were among the victims. He said he was paying tribute on behalf of Taiwan to those who died and their families.
Turning to regional security, Lee said China was rapidly expanding its nuclear arsenal and posed a serious threat to peace in the Taiwan Strait and the broader Indo-Pacific region.
Citing studies by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, the Federation of American Scientists and the Sasakawa Peace Foundation, he said China was the fastest-growing nuclear power and urged like-minded democracies to work together to safeguard global peace and stability.
According to the office, the Taiwanese delegation was seated in the diplomatic corps section alongside representatives from Paraguay, the Holy See, Israel, India and Armenia.
The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony is held annually on Aug. 6 to honor those who died when the United States dropped an atomic bomb on the city in 1945 in the closing stages of World War II.

items.body:
原话：“The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.”
论点：新的口服减肥药将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。

items.topic_zh: 新口服减肥药的积极影响
items.claim_zh: 新的口服减肥药将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。
items.article_body:
There’s a new kid on the block when it comes to weight loss treatments — and it’s set to give jabs a run for their money.
This week, the UK became the first country in Europe to approve the use of orforglipron — branded as Foundayo — for weight management and type 2 diabetes.
Made by Mounjaro manufacturer Eli Lilly, it’s one of two GLP-1 pills to receive Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) authorisation.
But while it’s got the go-ahead to be sold via private prescription, there’s no indication of whether Foundayo will be offered via the NHS.
Still, many experts are optimistic about the drug, with Dr Simon Cork, senior lecturer in physiology at Anglia Ruskin University, describing it as a ‘big step forward in the treatment of obesity.’
Glasgow University Professor of Metabolic Medicine, Naveed Sattar, added: ‘The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.’
Like semaglutide and tirzepatide (the active ingredients in Mounjaro, Wegovy and Ozempic ), orforglipron is a GLP-1 receptor agonist, which mimics a naturally occurring hormone, glucagon-like peptide released by the body after eating — just in the form of a pill to be taken once a day.
According to the MHRA, it ‘acts on areas of the brain that regulate appetite, helping people feel fuller for longer, reducing hunger and decreasing food cravings.’
At the same time, the medication regulates blood sugar, making it an effective treatment ‘for patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes.’
Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.
Foundayo is licensed for adults with insufficiently controlled diabetes, a BMI of 30 or above, or a BMI of between 27 and 30 and at least one weight-related comorbidity such as high blood pressure, heart disease, or obstructive sleep apnoea.
Dr Earim Chaudry, chief medical officer of Voy , tells Metro that people trialled on the highest dose of Foundayo lost an average of 12.4% of their body weight over 72 weeks, with around 1 in 5 participants without diabetes losing at least 20%.

Although results aren’t quite as dramatic as with jabs (Mounjaro users lose on average 22.5%) he says the pills can be a good alternative for ‘people who’ve been put off other weight loss medications, either because of needle anxiety or the food restrictions that some oral options require.’
‘Unlike the Wegovy pill, it can be taken at any time of day, with or without food, which offers more flexibility for people who want that,’ Dr Chaudry adds.
The MHRA lists the most common side effects for those taking orforglipron as nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting, indigestion, and abdominal pain.
Dr Chaudry notes that this is ‘consistent with other GLP-1 weight loss medications’, adding: ‘Stomach issues are common early on with this class of medicine, and tend to settle down as the body gets used to the medication and the dose, especially alongside small lifestyle adjustments.’
Anyone who suspects they’re having a side effect from this medicine is encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse, and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme .
While exact pricing may differ when Foundayo becomes available to buy later this month, Dr Simon Cork says it’s ‘likely to be much cheaper than currently available medications.’
Simple Online Pharmacy currently estimates a monthly supply will cost between £100 and £117, depending on dosage, but for those who sign up for a six-month plan with Voy, it’ll start from £69 each month.
In comparison, a minimum dose of Mounjaro currently comes in at £130 to £225 per month (not including introductory subscription discounts), with maintenance doses costing up to £359.

items.title_zh: 英国新口服减肥药Foundayo将比注射更便宜
items.summary_zh: 英国新推出的口服减肥药Foundayo被认为是一个积极的发展，预计将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。科学家指出，新的有效口服选择的出现，将使得减肥治疗更加普及，满足不同患者的需求。这一药物的推出可能会降低治疗成本，使得更多人能够负担得起，从而改善整体健康状况。
items.l1_lead: 英国新口服减肥药Foundayo的推出预计将降低治疗成本，使减肥治疗更加普及，满足不同患者的需求。
items.l2_summary: 英国新推出的口服减肥药Foundayo被视为减肥治疗领域的一个重要进展，预计将为更多人提供符合其需求和偏好的治疗选择。科学家们指出，口服药物的有效性和便利性将使减肥治疗更加普及，能够满足不同患者的需求。与传统的注射减肥药相比，Foundayo的推出可能会显著降低治疗成本，使得更多人能够负担得起这一治疗，从而有助于改善整体健康状况。这一新药的出现不仅为患者提供了更多的选择，也为减肥治疗的可及性和经济性带来了积极的影响，可能会改变人们对减肥药物的看法和使用方式。总的来说，Foundayo的上市标志着减肥治疗的一次重要革新，预示着未来在减肥药物领域可能会有更多创新和发展。

items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的管理，强调了简化生活方式建议的重要性。核心论点是，简化的饮食和活动建议能够帮助人们更有效地管理健康。作为支持这一观点的关键证据，作者提到他们正在与苏格兰政府合作，向所有临床医生提供简单易懂的饮食和活动建议。这一举措旨在改善患者的健康管理，推动2型糖尿病的治疗进入一个新的时代。
items.l1_lead: 简化饮食和活动建议能有效帮助2型糖尿病患者管理健康，推动治疗进入新纪元。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的管理，强调了简化生活方式建议的重要性。核心论点是，简化的饮食和活动建议能够帮助人们更有效地管理健康，从而改善2型糖尿病患者的生活质量。为了支持这一观点，作者提到他们正在与苏格兰政府合作，向所有临床医生提供简单易懂的饮食和活动建议。这一举措旨在通过降低患者在日常生活中对健康管理的复杂性，推动2型糖尿病的治疗进入一个新的时代。

通过提供清晰、易于理解的指导，患者能够更好地遵循健康的生活方式，从而有效控制血糖水平，减少并发症的风险。简化的建议不仅能够提高患者的依从性，还能使临床医生在日常诊疗中更高效地传达健康信息。这种方法的实施，标志着对2型糖尿病管理的重新思考，强调了生活方式在疾病控制中的关键作用。

总之，本文呼吁在2型糖尿病的治疗中，采用更为简化和易于执行的生活方式建议，以期改善患者的健康管理效果，推动治疗方法的创新与进步。

items.title: Nanomedicine-Based Therapeutic Strategies for Next-Generation Cancer Immunotherapy.
items.body: Cancer immunotherapy has reshaped cancer treatment by enabling the immune system to recognize and eliminate tumor cells. Nevertheless, its clinical translation remains limited by suboptimal response rates, poor penetration into deep tumor tissues, and insufficient therapeutic efficacy. Cancer immunotherapy alone is often inadequate as a sole treatment modality. Nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies, including photothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, nanozyme-based therapy, and cancer vaccines, have achieved considerable recognition for cancer treatment. Upon integration with cancer immunotherapy or regulated cell death pathways, these nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies can modulate the tumor microenvironment, enhance anticancer immune response, and overcome immunotherapy resistance. This article summarizes recent advances in nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies, the role of cancer immunotherapy, and regulated cell death pathways. We outline the strengths and limitations of these therapeutic strategies. We also discuss how combination therapeutic strategies achieve synergistic effects, future challenges, and perspectives in developing next-generation nanomedicine platforms for cancer immunotherapy.
items.authors: Tan BSN, Zhao Y, Zhao Y.
items.title_zh: 基于纳米医学的下一代癌症免疫治疗策略
items.summary_zh: 癌症免疫治疗通过激活免疫系统识别和消灭肿瘤细胞，重塑了癌症治疗。然而，其临床应用受到反应率低、深层肿瘤组织渗透性差和疗效不足的限制。单独的癌症免疫治疗往往不足以作为唯一治疗手段。基于纳米医学的治疗策略，如光热疗法、光动力疗法、声动力疗法、纳米酶治疗和癌症疫苗，已在癌症治疗中获得显著认可。与癌症免疫治疗或调控细胞死亡途径结合后，这些策略能够调节肿瘤微环境，增强抗癌免疫反应，并克服免疫治疗耐药性。本文总结了基于纳米医学的治疗策略的最新进展、癌症免疫治疗的作用及调控细胞死亡途径，分析了这些策略的优缺点，并讨论了组合治疗策略如何实现协同效应、未来挑战及发展下一代纳米医学平台的前景。
items.l1_lead: 基于纳米医学的治疗策略与癌症免疫治疗结合，能够有效增强抗癌免疫反应，克服免疫治疗耐药性，推动癌症治疗的进步。
items.l2_summary:
癌症免疫治疗通过激活免疫系统来识别和消灭肿瘤细胞，已经在癌症治疗领域取得了显著进展。然而，其临床应用面临反应率低、深层肿瘤组织渗透性差和疗效不足等限制，单独使用癌症免疫治疗往往难以作为唯一的治疗手段。为了解决这些问题，基于纳米医学的治疗策略逐渐受到重视，包括光热疗法、光动力疗法、声动力疗法、纳米酶治疗和癌症疫苗等。这些纳米医学策略在癌症治疗中展现出显著的潜力，尤其是当它们与癌症免疫治疗或调控细胞死亡途径相结合时，能够有效调节肿瘤微环境，增强抗癌免疫反应，并克服免疫治疗的耐药性。

在最新的研究中，基于纳米医学的治疗策略被认为能够通过改善药物的靶向性和生物相容性，提升治疗效果。这些策略不仅可以增强免疫细胞对肿瘤细胞的识别能力，还能通过调节肿瘤微环境，促进免疫细胞的浸润和活化。具体而言，光热疗法和光动力疗法能够通过局部加热或光照杀死肿瘤细胞，从而释放抗原，激活免疫反应；声动力疗法则利用超声波增强药物的渗透性；纳米酶治疗通过模拟酶的功能，促进肿瘤细胞的死亡；癌症疫苗则通过训练免疫系统识别肿瘤特异性抗原。

然而，这些纳米医学策略也存在一定的局限性，例如在临床应用中的复杂性和潜在的副作用。因此，研究者们正在探索组合治疗策略，以实现协同效应，最大化治疗效果。通过将纳米医学策略与传统的癌症免疫治疗相结合，未来有望克服当前治疗中的挑战，提升患者的生存率和生活质量。

综上所述，基于纳米医学的下一代癌症免疫治疗策略展现出广阔的前景，尽管仍面临一些挑战，但通过不断的研究和技术进步，这些策略有望为癌症患者带来新的希望。

items.title: The South’s aging water infrastructure is getting pounded by climate change – fixing it is also a struggle
items.body: Extreme downpours and droughts, both fueled by rising global temperatures, are taking a toll. Communities trying to manage the threats face three big challenges.
items.authors: John C. Morris
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/john-c-morris-1526386（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 南方老化水利基础设施受气候变化冲击，修复面临挑战
items.summary_zh: 随着全球气温上升，极端降雨和干旱现象愈发频繁，给南方地区的水利基础设施带来了严重影响。社区在应对这些威胁时面临三大挑战：基础设施老化、资金不足以及气候变化带来的不确定性。这些因素共同加剧了水资源管理的困难，迫使地方政府和相关机构不得不寻找有效的解决方案，以应对日益严峻的气候变化带来的影响。
items.l1_lead: 南方老化水利基础设施在气候变化的影响下面临极端天气挑战，修复工作因老化、资金不足和不确定性而愈加困难。
items.l2_summary:
随着全球气温的上升，南方地区的水利基础设施正面临着气候变化带来的严重冲击，尤其是极端降雨和干旱现象的频繁发生。这些气候变化的影响使得原本就老化的水利基础设施更加脆弱，导致了水资源管理的困难加剧。社区在应对这些威胁时，主要面临三大挑战：首先是基础设施的老化，许多水利设施已经使用多年，亟需修复和升级；其次是资金不足，地方政府和相关机构在面对修复需求时，往往缺乏足够的财政支持，限制了有效应对的能力；最后，气候变化带来的不确定性使得水资源管理的规划和实施变得更加复杂，难以预测未来的水文变化和极端天气事件。

这些因素共同作用，迫使地方政府和相关机构必须积极寻找有效的解决方案，以应对日益严峻的气候变化影响。面对基础设施老化和资金短缺的问题，地方政府需要探索新的融资模式和合作机制，以确保水利基础设施的可持续发展。同时，针对气候变化的不确定性，相关机构应加强对气候数据的监测和分析，以便更好地制定应对策略和管理措施。总之，南方地区的水利基础设施在气候变化的冲击下，亟需综合考虑老化、资金和不确定性等多重因素，以实现有效的修复和管理，保障水资源的安全和可持续利用。
items.l3_translation:
气候变化正在威胁美国的水基础设施，越来越强烈的风暴使社区遭受洪水侵袭，而干旱则在没有准备的地区耗尽了淡水供应。

2024年4月席卷南方的严重风暴展示了一些风险：在新奥尔良，降雨速度远远超过了城市泵的排水能力。在密西西比州哈蒂斯堡附近，风暴期间一条水管破裂。其他社区则面临停电和在使用水之前需煮沸以确保安全的建议。

我们研究基础设施的韧性和可持续性，看到危机正在加剧，特别是在美国东南部，老化的供水系统和雨水基础设施使更多社区面临风险，因为天气变得越来越极端。

为了找到最佳解决方案并建设韧性基础设施，社区需要认识到在变暖的世界中面临的威胁以及管理这些威胁的障碍。

水危机可能由水过多或水过少引起，并且可能以意想不到的方式挑战饮用水系统。

在过去十年中，阿拉巴马州北部和中部的部分地区经历了严重的干旱。此外，由于干旱和过度使用的结合，挖掘的水井也干涸了，水位下降。

2023年，新奥尔良的水供应以另一种方式受到干旱的威胁：由于密西西比河的水流减缓，来自墨西哥湾的盐水侵入河流的范围比正常情况更远。

与此同时，倾盆大雨事件越来越多地压垮了雨水系统，威胁到饮用水供应。随着全球气温上升，海洋变暖，这种温暖的水为强烈风暴提供了更多的水分。

密西西比州杰克逊市的情况就是极端局势的一个例子，这座城市有近15万居民。在2022年之前，杰克逊的水系统已经受到泄漏和管道破裂的困扰超过十年，直到强烈的洪水压垮了系统，使大多数居民在数天内几乎没有水可用。

即使在洪水发生之前，杰克逊的居民也被建议在饮用水之前先煮沸。现在，借助8亿美元的联邦税款，维修工作正在进行中，但关于如何在未来保持系统维护的问题仍然存在。4月的风暴再次袭击该地区，带来了破坏性的风、降雨和停电。

老化水基础设施的脆弱性在许多社区中显而易见。美国土木工程师学会在2021年的美国基础设施报告卡中估计，美国每两分钟就有一处水管破裂，每天损失60亿加仑的处理水。工程师们给美国市政水系统的总体评分为C-。

洪水防护基础设施的评分甚至更低：美国的堤坝和水坝均获得D级，并警告说，扩展开发意味着更多的人和财产在下游，依赖堤坝和水坝的正常运作。

如今的基础设施从砖瓦建筑到电子网络不等——每种基础设施都有不同的需求、目标、责任和对气候变化的脆弱性。

此外，基础设施往往是相互依赖的。如果一个资产发生故障，例如管道或控制水处理厂的计算机系统，损害可能会波及到其他系统。例如，由于系统故障而排放到溪流中的未经处理的废水可能会影响下游社区的饮用水供应。

水问题跨越不同级别的政府、法律和法规，以及技术和学术专业知识，要求建立可能难以管理的合作伙伴关系。这可能导致不同政府机构之间的冲突，因为在联邦、州和地方政府之间，关于监管控制和责任的争议不断出现。

在许多地区，几个世纪以来建立的水基础设施塑造了随后的发展决策、可用资源和土地使用模式，包括新住宅、交通设施和商业的选址。

如今，这些基础设施也可能以其开发者从未想象过的方式受到气候变化的威胁。

更强烈的降雨事件使某些地区长期以来的洪水地图变得过时，而以前从未被认为有洪水风险的地区现在却经常发生洪水。这在沿海地区尤其如此，风暴可能与异常高的潮汐、海平面上升和沉降相结合。

关于谁为基础设施改善买单，或者谁决定项目优先级的问题也可能引发冲突。

基础设施是昂贵的。单个项目，例如更换水管或处理设施，将涉及显著的设计和建设成本，以及许多贫困社区难以承担的维护和修理费用。

美国土木工程师学会在2021年估计，2020年代十年间所需的各类基础设施投资（5.9万亿美元）与计划和资助的基础设施工作（3.3万亿美元）之间的差额为2.6万亿美元。预计到2029年，仅饮用水和废水投资的年度缺口将达到4340亿美元。

建设新的、气候韧性的基础设施超出了许多社区，特别是低收入社区的财务能力。

联邦政府近年来采取了措施提供更多援助。2021年通过的《两党基础设施法》授权为饮用水、废水、水储存和水再利用项目提供550亿美元。次年通过的《通货膨胀削减法》包括5.5亿美元，用于帮助弱势社区进行水供应项目。

但这些资金并不能弥补缺口，减少联邦支出的政治压力使得未来联邦对基础设施的支持变得不确定。

地方社区、州和联邦机构需要重新审视来自老化基础设施的日益威胁。

items.title: Sewage testing robots process wastewater faster to predict COVID 19 outbreaks sooner
items.body: A community’s wastewater can predict coronavirus cases that haven’t yet been diagnosed. The quicker that information is known, the better.
items.authors: Rob Knight
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/rob-knight-1215921（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 污水检测机器人加速处理废水以预测COVID-19疫情
items.summary_zh: 社区的废水能够预测尚未确诊的冠状病毒病例。通过污水监测，科学家们可以更快地获取疫情信息，从而提前采取防控措施。这种方法的关键在于污水中病毒的浓度变化，能够反映出社区内的感染情况。研究表明，及时获取这些数据可以显著提高疫情响应的效率，帮助公共卫生部门更好地应对疫情。因此，污水检测机器人在处理废水和分析数据方面的快速能力，将为预测COVID-19疫情提供更为有效的支持。
items.l1_lead: 污水检测机器人通过监测废水中的病毒浓度变化，能够快速预测社区内的COVID-19疫情，从而提高疫情响应效率。
items.l2_summary: 污水检测机器人在废水处理和数据分析方面的快速能力，为预测COVID-19疫情提供了有效支持。研究表明，社区的废水中病毒浓度的变化能够反映出该地区的感染情况，从而帮助科学家更快地获取疫情信息。这种污水监测方法能够提前识别尚未确诊的冠状病毒病例，使公共卫生部门能够及时采取防控措施。通过及时获取污水中病毒的数据，疫情响应的效率显著提高，进而增强了公共卫生系统对疫情的应对能力。因此，污水检测机器人在这一过程中发挥了重要作用，成为监测和预测疫情的重要工具。
items.l3_translation:
研究简报是关于有趣学术工作的简短介绍。

通过使用污水处理机器人，我们的实验室能够以比非自动化的大规模系统快30倍的速度在废水中检测到冠状病毒。这一进展发表在微生物学期刊《mSystems》上，为监测废水以获取COVID-19地方病例早期预警的社区提供了更多的提前时间。

当临床研究显示检测出SARS-CoV-2阳性的人在其粪便中排出病毒时，污水似乎是寻找病毒的显而易见的地方。废水监测可以在社区层面上使用，以便在临床诊断之前观察潜在的疫情聚集，特别是在COVID-19流行率远高于检测率的地区。

问题在于，由于许多人的卫生间排水汇入污水，病毒在废水流中被严重稀释，更不用说他们冲洗的其他垃圾。监测依赖于从废水中浓缩病毒颗粒，以检测这些低水平。这一病毒浓缩步骤通常是废水分析中的主要瓶颈，因为它费时费力。我们的机器人系统采取了一种不同且更快速的方法。

全国各地的城市、学校和企业正在使用废水监测来发现他们周围的冠状病毒。

废水监测作为高风险地区的早期警报系统尤其有用，例如在那些无证居民可能对个人检测持谨慎态度的社区。

最常用的病毒浓缩技术使用过滤器，可能需要六到八个小时才能将几十个污水样本转化为可以测试SARS-CoV-2存在的样本。我们的新协议在一次40分钟的运行中浓缩24个样本。

我们重新利用通常在实验室中执行微生物学或细胞生物学任务的设备来处理污水。通过微型化和自动化我们的系统，我们消除了许多劳动密集型步骤、资源和相关成本。而且我们的无接触过程要快得多。

我们从圣地亚哥主要污水处理厂的自动取样器收集污水，以及从我们在加利福尼亚大学圣地亚哥分校校园内100多个检查井中部署的设备，这些设备每30分钟收集一次污水样本。

然后，在实验室中，我们不依赖多个过滤步骤，而是使用微小的磁珠来富集病毒颗粒。我们购买了这些设计用于结合多种呼吸道病毒的纳米磁珠。污水处理机器人配备了一个专用的磁头，可以抓取附着有病毒的磁珠。它优先捕捉病毒颗粒，留下污水样本中的其他杂质。

使用机器人自动化污水浓缩过程使我们能够在每个机器人中在40分钟内浓缩24个样本。然后，同一台机器人可以提取病毒RNA，在36分钟内处理96个样本。最后，我们使用聚合酶链反应来搜索SARS-CoV-2的特征基因，类似于实验室对患者鼻拭子的临床诊断测试。

总体而言，我们的系统可以在4.5小时内处理96个样本，显著减少从样本到结果的时间。

到目前为止，我们的研究是我们所知的唯一使用自动化过程的冠状病毒废水研究。

我们正在将这一技术作为我们校园大规模废水监测的一部分，每天在100多个地点进行取样。圣地亚哥学区也将其作为早期警报系统使用。

我们现在正在使用系统的病毒基因组测序部分来追踪新SARS-CoV-2变种的出现。

items.title: What are the symptoms of omicron?
items.body: Omicron is continuing the trend set by delta, causing symptoms that resemble the common cold.
items.authors: Tim D. Spector
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 奥密克戎的症状是什么？
items.summary_zh: 奥密克戎（Omicron）继续延续德尔塔（Delta）变种的趋势，导致的症状与普通感冒相似。这一现象引发了科学界的关注，研究表明，奥密克戎感染者常出现咳嗽、喉咙痛、流鼻涕等症状，且这些症状通常较轻。与之前的变种相比，奥密克戎的传播速度更快，但其引发的严重疾病风险相对较低。科学家们指出，尽管症状相似，但仍需保持警惕，特别是在高风险人群中，疫苗接种和防护措施仍然至关重要。
items.l1_lead: 奥密克戎感染者的症状类似普通感冒，传播速度快但严重疾病风险较低，仍需对高风险人群保持警惕。
items.l2_summary: 奥密克戎（Omicron）变种的出现引发了科学界的广泛关注，其症状与普通感冒相似，继续延续了德尔塔（Delta）变种的趋势。研究表明，感染奥密克戎的患者常常出现咳嗽、喉咙痛和流鼻涕等症状，这些症状通常较轻，且与以往变种相比，奥密克戎的传播速度显著加快。然而，尽管其引发的严重疾病风险相对较低，科学家们仍然强调对这一变种保持警惕，尤其是在高风险人群中。疫苗接种和防护措施在控制疫情传播中依然至关重要。因此，尽管奥密克戎的症状较轻，公众仍需关注自身健康状况，并采取必要的预防措施，以降低感染风险。
items.l3_translation:
近两年来，数百万公众成员每天向ZOE COVID研究提交健康报告，帮助我们追踪疫情的发展。特别是通过该研究应用程序提交的4.8亿份报告显示，随着病毒的演变，其引起的症状也在变化。

早在2020年，原始和阿尔法版本的冠状病毒迅速显现出三种非常常见的症状——咳嗽、发热和嗅觉丧失——以及至少20种其他症状。这些症状包括疲劳、头痛、呼吸急促、肌肉疼痛和胃肠问题，还有一些较为不寻常的现象，如皮疹和“COVID舌”。

当德尔塔变种出现时，我们注意到最常报告的症状发生了变化。之前常见的症状，如呼吸急促、发热和嗅觉丧失，排名下降。感冒样症状——包括流鼻涕、喉咙痛和持续打喷嚏——变得更加普遍，尤其是在接种过疫苗的人群中，头痛和咳嗽也变得更为常见。

奥密克戎似乎在延续德尔塔所设定的趋势。它引起的症状更像是普通感冒，尤其是在接种过疫苗的人中，系统性症状（如恶心、肌肉疼痛、腹泻和皮疹）则较少。

我们查看了在12月报告感染COVID的人们的健康报告，当时奥密克戎在英国传播，并将其与10月初的数据进行了比较，当时德尔塔是主要变种。然后，我们通过分析一小组被政府告知其阳性PCR结果被怀疑或确认是奥密克戎感染的贡献者的数据来验证我们的比较结果。

我们的分析显示，德尔塔和奥密克戎的整体症状特征没有显著差异，在这两个时间段内，前五种症状都是流鼻涕、头痛、疲劳、打喷嚏和喉咙痛。但在症状的整体流行程度上，有一些明显的差异。

例如，嗅觉丧失（嗅觉或味觉丧失）在10月时位列前十，但现在已降至第17位。曾经是COVID的关键指标的症状，现在仅在约五分之一的阳性检测者中出现。根据我们的数据，少于三分之一的人（29%）会经历发热，这也远低于我们过去看到的情况。

重要的是，我们发现只有一半的COVID患者有发热、咳嗽或嗅觉丧失这三种经典症状，这表明政府关于PCR检测的指导（建议如果出现这三种症状之一就应进行检测）已经严重过时。

这种新变种的传染性远高于之前的变种，导致英国及其他国家病例激增。尽管尚不清楚我们是否会面临因该疾病而导致的住院潮，但重要的是要记住，虽然奥密克戎和德尔塔对我们许多人来说可能感觉像感冒，但它仍然可能致命或导致长期症状，干扰日常生活，尤其是对于未接种疫苗或免疫系统受损的人。

到目前为止，我们看到大多数病例出现在年轻人中，但在整体感染率仍然如此高的情况下，老年人群体的病例也在上升。75岁以上人群阳性病例的最近上升令人担忧，但我们希望英国老年人和更脆弱群体的高疫苗接种率将继续转化为更轻微的症状和较少的住院病例。奥密克戎的主要问题更多是它在关键医疗人员中造成的缺勤潮。

随着我们在英国进入冬季深处，一些相当严重的感冒正在传播，还有常年流行的流感。ZOE COVID研究应用程序的数据告诉我们，目前COVID变种引起的症状与普通感冒非常相似。这意味着仅凭症状无法确定你得了什么。当COVID的传播率很高时，新的喉咙痛、流鼻涕或异常疲劳应被视为COVID，直到你接受检测。

由于ZOE COVID研究应用程序的贡献者记录他们每天经历的任何症状以及任何COVID检测结果，我们还能够追踪非COVID感冒的流行情况。就在三个月前，约每12个有新呼吸道症状的人中就有一个检测出COVID阳性。然而，随着奥密克戎的出现，目前约50%的“新感冒”实际上是COVID。

因此，如果你或家人感到不适，尤其是如果你经常流鼻涕和打喷嚏，那么很有可能是COVID。你应该待在家里并进行检测以确认。请记住，尽管快速抗原检测效果不错，尤其是如果你同时取样喉咙和鼻子，但它们的敏感性低于PCR检测。当你进行一次检测时，尽量在接下来的几天重复进行，因为单次阴性的快速抗原检测并不能保证你没有感染。

最后，无论政府的指导如何，无论你是否感染了COVID，如果你感到身体不适，出现奇怪或感冒样的症状，最好待在家里，并在外出时避免接触他人，佩戴口罩，以避免将病菌传播给可能更脆弱的人。

伦敦国王学院的遗传流行病学研究

某人是数据科学和营养公司ZOE Ltd的联合创始人，该公司运营ZOE COVID研究。该研究获得英国卫生与社会护理部的资助。某人从他所著的书籍《饮食神话》和《喂养》获得版税。

伦敦国王学院作为《对话》英国的成员提供资金支持。

items.title: Should we all be using ‘sniff tests’ to screen for COVID 19?
items.body: Temperature checks have become a commonplace screening tool for COVID-19, but loss of sense of smell is a more predictive symptom of coronavirus infection than fever.
items.authors: Tim D. Spector
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 我们是否都应该使用“嗅觉测试”筛查COVID-19？
items.summary_zh: 温度检测已成为COVID-19的常见筛查工具，但失去嗅觉的症状比发热更能预测冠状病毒感染。研究表明，嗅觉丧失是COVID-19感染的一个重要指标，可能比传统的体温监测更有效。因此，科学家建议在筛查COVID-19时，考虑使用嗅觉测试作为补充手段，以提高早期发现感染者的能力。这一观点强调了嗅觉测试在公共卫生应对中的潜在价值，尤其是在疫情高发时期。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，嗅觉丧失是COVID-19感染的重要指标，建议在筛查中使用嗅觉测试以提高早期发现感染者的能力。
items.l2_summary: 温度检测已成为COVID-19（新冠病毒）筛查的常见工具，但研究表明，嗅觉丧失（anosmia）这一症状在预测冠状病毒感染方面的有效性更高。相关研究指出，嗅觉丧失是COVID-19感染的重要指标，甚至可能比传统的体温监测更具预测能力。这一发现促使科学家们建议在COVID-19筛查中，考虑将嗅觉测试作为一种补充手段，以提高早期发现感染者的能力。尤其是在疫情高发时期，嗅觉测试的潜在价值愈发凸显。通过引入嗅觉测试，公共卫生应对措施有望更加精准，从而有效控制疫情的传播。因此，重视嗅觉测试在筛查中的应用，可能为公共卫生政策提供新的思路和方法。
items.l3_translation:
控制COVID-19传播的最佳方法之一是迅速识别感染冠状病毒的人，并防止他们将病毒传播给他人。

目前，体温检测被作为一种公共筛查工具，用于识别感染COVID-19的人，像台湾这样的国家将体温检测作为其控制措施的关键组成部分。然而，几乎没有科学证据表明体温检测能够可靠地检测COVID-19。

首先，手持扫描仪仅测量皮肤温度，而不是核心体温，皮肤温度可能会有所波动，并且设备的可靠性存在问题。来自ZOE COVID症状研究应用的数据表明，超过一半（57%）检测出COVID-19阳性的人从未出现发热，而那些确实有体温升高的人平均只有两天的时间。机场的体温筛查未能检测到大多数感染者并不令人惊讶。

如果使用体温检测来检测COVID可能只提供一种虚假的安全感，那么我们应该做些什么呢？

来自我们应用的400万用户的数据帮助我们确认，嗅觉丧失（嗅觉缺失）是4月COVID-19的一个关键症状。我们为促使英国和其他国家将其作为官方症状做出了贡献。我的同事和我在《柳叶刀》上撰写的最新应用数据中强调，65%的COVID-19阳性成年人报告嗅觉丧失，其中相当一部分人从未经历过体温升高，而仅有40%多的阳性检测者有发热症状。

对于大约16%的阳性检测者来说，嗅觉丧失是他们唯一的症状。重要的是，在COVID-19感染期间，嗅觉缺失持续约七天，通常更长，而大多数人的发热仅持续三天。

此外，伦敦大学学院的科学家进行的一项研究显示，在病毒第一波期间，超过75%报告嗅觉丧失的人检测出冠状病毒抗体，尽管其中四分之一的人没有表现出其他经典症状。

总体而言，数据表明，嗅觉的突然丧失是COVID-19在所有年龄组中比发热更常见的早期症状。对于年轻人来说，它是COVID-19阳性检测的20倍更好的预测指标，对于老年人来说，是13倍更好的指示。

基于这些发现，在机场和酒店等场所使用“嗅觉测试”而不是体温检测可能是更好的广泛筛查方式。虽然理论上这似乎是个好主意，但不幸的是，这里有一个问题。

首先，嗅觉减退相当普遍。近20%的成年人有某种程度的嗅觉丧失，而这一数字在75岁以上的人群中上升至80%。这些人不太可能有任何证明其先前嗅觉丧失的证据，以使他们免于嗅觉测试的限制。

其次，当我们查看应用的数据时，我们发现大多数人在感染COVID-19后大约需要一周才能恢复嗅觉。但大约十分之一的人嗅觉丧失持续三周或更长时间——这远远超过他们可能具有传染性的时间。

最后，许多人在因普通感冒、鼻窦炎或花粉症而鼻塞时会失去嗅觉。尽管鼻塞并不被视为COVID-19的症状，但简单的嗅觉测试可能无法区分这两者。

这意味着，尽管嗅觉测试可能在感染时识别出COVID-19患者，但也会有大量非传染性的人同样未能通过测试，并面临不必要的限制。

因此，虽然“嗅觉测试”可能不是答案，但嗅觉的突然变化仍然可能是COVID-19早期感染的最佳指示。我们的应用显示这一症状在儿童中较少见，但这可能是因为他们在未经过测试的情况下不太可能注意到。

检查嗅觉的变化很简单，可以通过简单的家庭香味物品（如咖啡、柠檬、香草或臭奶酪）每天在家中进行。如果你发现自己或孩子的嗅觉发生了突然变化，而这种变化对你来说并不正常，你应该尽快自我隔离并进行COVID-19检测。

ZOE COVID症状研究应用可以从Apple App Store和Google Play Store下载。研究更新和数据可以在covid.joinzoe.com/找到。

伦敦国王学院的遗传流行病学教授

某某人获得了来自多个来源的资助，包括威康信托、医学研究理事会、国家健康研究院、CDRF、Seerave基金会、达能、ZOE、BHF。ZOE CSS应用是非营利性项目。他是ZOE Global Ltd的联合创始人，并且是两本关于营养的书籍的作者；《饮食神话》（Orion 2016）和《喂养——我们被告知的关于食物的绝大多数都是错误的》（某某人 2020）。

伦敦国王学院作为《对话》英国的成员提供资金支持。

撰写文章并加入一个由超过234,300名来自5,629个机构的学者和研究人员组成的不断壮大的社区。
